title: Remove Nth From End
statement:
Delete the k-th node counted from the end of a singly linked list and return the resulting head.

Contract
- `head` points to the first node of a non-empty acyclic list. Each node has an integer `value` and a mutable `next` reference.
- `k` is 1-based and always valid: 1 removes the last node and the list length removes the head.
- Return the head of the list after removal; this is null when the only node was removed.
- Relink the existing nodes instead of allocating replacements, and do it in a single pass without first counting the length.

Examples
- Removing the 2nd node from the end of `1 -> 2 -> 3 -> 4 -> 5` gives `1 -> 2 -> 3 -> 5`.
- Removing the 1st node from the end of `7` returns null.
- Removing the 2nd node from the end of `1 -> 2` returns the node holding `2`.
hints: Counting the length first needs two passes; try keeping two pointers a fixed distance apart instead.
Move a lead pointer k nodes ahead, then move both pointers together until the lead reaches the last node.
A sentinel node in front of the head lets you remove the head without a special case. Intended complexity: O(n) time and O(1) extra space, where n is the number of nodes.
inputSyntax: Input: the list values followed by k, for example: [1, 2, 3, 4, 5] 2
